product_from_film: Palmier presents a video editor that Claude can use to organize media, assemble an edit and generate footage.
explains_well: The film shows its own opening footage inside the editor after the organize and edit prompts.
unclear: Actual execution time, reliability, amount of manual work and generation quality across cases are not established.
scenario: Ask Claude to organize media and edit it, then generate eye close-ups and show the output in a timeline.
product_clear_basis: Opening text says we built Claude its own video editor; dock labels and the editor UI reinforce this at 5–6s.

categories.finding: The film names the editor, organizes media, edits its own opening, adds generation and ends with the URL.
A carried laptop and we built Claude text start the claim; its own video editor completes the purpose around 2s.
Claude-assisted video editing is named early, with practical organization and editing tasks at 9–23s.
Typed prompt states, timeline changes and reference/output changes are visible. Exact editing speed and camera-zoom generation motion need denser evidence.
Live-action-style setup alternates with tight chat/editor crops, black question cards and reaction faces.
Dark software surfaces contrast with warm desk footage and varied close eye textures.
Short prompts are enlarged, while detailed tool responses and timeline labels are small and quick.
Voice delivery is unverified.

Effects and their sources are unverified.

categories.finding: Prompts, folders, timeline and recognizable opening footage make the broad workflow readable without sound.
The sequence moves attention from prompt to tool response to editor result; the same laptop shot confirms continuity.
Three capabilities fit into about 30s of demonstration. The eye prompt adds a concrete example but generation quality has little inspection time.
The opening editor claim is answered by showing the opening scene assembled inside that editor.
Reaction faces and casual captions may create surprise and informality; viewer response is unmeasured.
The opening laptop and desk shots reappear in the timeline and preview, linking finished film to demo assets.
Prompt, tool-call and resulting editor states are shown. Reliability, actual latency, full automation and general output quality are untested.
The self-referential timeline demo is specific to this editor; application names and URL identify the brand.
A short hold on one before/after eye result would add useful quality evidence beyond a rapid output montage.
categories.experiment: Hold the source eye reference and one generated close-up side by side for three seconds.

categories.finding: For Tin, show the current launch asset inside the product workflow so the demo outcome is already familiar.
categories.experiment: Start with a finished campaign image, then reveal its brief and actual saved output in Tin.

categories.finding: No human new-viewer test was performed.
categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

categories.finding: Mobile preview and accessibility checks were not performed.

lessons.keep: Reuse the opening footage inside the demonstrated editor to make the result easy to recognize.
try: Hold one eye reference beside its generated result for three seconds so viewers can inspect consistency.
For Tin, open with a completed campaign asset, then show that exact asset being made and saved from its brief.
lessons.avoid: Inferring execution speed or full automation from a compressed sequence of tool and editor states.
lessons.open: Manual work, processing time, generation reliability, export quality and audio remain unverified.
